sections.instruction: Complete the sentences using PERFECT MODALS:

questions.prompt: We didn’t go out last night. We [gap] (go) to the cinema but we decided to stay at home.
acceptedAnswers: could have gone|might have gone

questions.prompt: Jerry passed the examination. He didn’t study very much for it. The exam [gap] (be) very difficult.
acceptedAnswers: can't have been|couldn't have been

questions.prompt: A: I wonder where Tom was going when you saw him. B: He [gap] (go) to work.
acceptedAnswers: must have been going|may have been going|might have been going|could have been going
questions.explanation: past deduction, continuous: must have been + -ing

questions.prompt: Thank you for doing the washing-up but you [gap] (do) it really. I was going to do it later.
acceptedAnswers: needn't have done|need not have done
questions.explanation: unnecessary past action: needn’t have + V3

questions.prompt: The driver in front stopped suddenly without warning and I drove into the back of his car. It wasn’t my fault. He [gap] (give) warning that he was going to stop.
acceptedAnswers: should have given|ought to have given

questions.prompt: A: How do you think the fire started? B: Well, I suppose someone [gap] (drop) a cigarette.
acceptedAnswers: might have dropped|may have dropped|must have dropped|could have dropped

questions.prompt: A: What time is it? B: Well, we came at seven, and I’m sure we’ve been here for at least an hour. So it [gap] (be) around eight o’clock.
acceptedAnswers: must be

questions.prompt: A: Jack was absent yesterday afternoon. Where was he? B: I don’t know. He [gap] (go) to a movie or he [gap] (be) at home.
acceptedAnswers: may have gone|might have gone|could have gone / may have been|might have been|could have been

questions.prompt: I had a test this morning. I didn’t do well on the test because I didn’t study for it last night. I [gap] (study) it.
acceptedAnswers: should have studied|ought to have studied

sections.instruction: Fill in the blanks using MUST (HAVE), CAN’T (HAVE), MAY-MIGHT-COULD (HAVE):

questions.prompt: She knew everything about our plans. She [gap] (listen) to our conversation.
acceptedAnswers: must have listened|must have been listening

questions.prompt: He [gap] (eat) the roasted beef when we were out. He is a vegetarian.
acceptedAnswers: can't have eaten|couldn't have eaten

questions.prompt: Mrs. White bought a new fur coat! She [gap] (win) a lottery.
acceptedAnswers: must have won|may have won|might have won|could have won

questions.prompt: John said he would ring, but he hasn’t. He [gap] (forget) all about it.
acceptedAnswers: must have forgotten|may have forgotten|might have forgotten|could have forgotten

questions.prompt: It is possible that he wasn’t taken to the cinema last weekend. He [gap] (not / take) to the cinema.
acceptedAnswers: may not have been taken|might not have been taken
questions.explanation: passive past possibility: may not have been + V3

questions.prompt: The children [gap] (study) in the library now, because they have a test tomorrow.
acceptedAnswers: must be studying|may be studying|might be studying|could be studying

questions.prompt: The singer has got a sore throat, so she [gap] (sing) at the concert.
acceptedAnswers: can't sing|couldn't sing|may not sing|might not sing

questions.prompt: I [gap] (be) at home this evening or I [gap] (be) but I’m not sure.
acceptedAnswers: may be|might be|could be / may not be|might not be
questions.explanation: possibility: may be / may not be

sections.instruction: Rewrite the following sentences using MUST / CAN’T / MAY / MIGHT with the suitable infinitive forms (+ infinitive or + perfect infinitive) according to their tenses:

questions.prompt: It is possible that they will not reach agreement.
acceptedAnswers: They may not reach agreement.
They might not reach agreement.

questions.prompt: Perhaps you found you made a mistake.
acceptedAnswers: You may have found you made a mistake.
You may have found you had made a mistake.
You may have found that you made a mistake.
You may have found that you had made a mistake.
You might have found you made a mistake.
You might have found you had made a mistake.
You might have found that you made a mistake.
You might have found that you had made a mistake.
You could have found you made a mistake.
You could have found you had made a mistake.
You could have found that you made a mistake.
You could have found that you had made a mistake.

questions.prompt: It is certain that our boss will give a rise in our salary.
acceptedAnswers: Our boss must give a rise in our salary.

questions.prompt: It is impossible that she won the beauty contest last year.
acceptedAnswers: She can't have won the beauty contest last year.
She couldn't have won the beauty contest last year.

questions.prompt: Perhaps parents will find that they cannot understand the new teaching methods being introduced in primary schools.
acceptedAnswers: Parents may find that they cannot understand the new teaching methods being introduced in primary schools.
Parents might find that they cannot understand the new teaching methods being introduced in primary schools.
Parents could find that they cannot understand the new teaching methods being introduced in primary schools.

questions.prompt: It is not impossible that the Government’s policy will prove to be little short of disastrous.
acceptedAnswers: The Government’s policy may prove to be little short of disastrous.
The Government’s policy might prove to be little short of disastrous.
The Government’s policy could prove to be little short of disastrous.

questions.prompt: I’m sure Jane got 5 in her last exam.
acceptedAnswers: Jane must have got 5 in her last exam.

questions.prompt: I’m sure you will catch the 5 o’clock train.
acceptedAnswers: You must catch the 5 o’clock train.

questions.prompt: It is possible that he changed his mind after I had offered him the job.
acceptedAnswers: He may have changed his mind after I had offered him the job.
He might have changed his mind after I had offered him the job.
He could have changed his mind after I had offered him the job.

questions.prompt: I’m sure Tom didn’t visit his parents last year because he was abroad and very busy.
acceptedAnswers: Tom can't have visited his parents last year because he was abroad and very busy.
Tom couldn't have visited his parents last year because he was abroad and very busy.

sections.instruction: Complete the responses to the statements, using MUST or CAN’T to suggest what seems to be the most likely explanation. Write the whole response:

questions.prompt: His fiancée writes him every day. → She must
questions.modelAnswer: She must love him very much.

questions.prompt: I don’t seem to have my key with me. → I must
questions.modelAnswer: I must have left it at home.

questions.prompt: He drives a Rolls-Royce and his wife a Mercedes. → They must
He has no idea what the book is about. → He can’t
He talks about going to the moon next year. → He must
She didn’t reply to his letter. → She can’t
He wears glasses all the time. → His eyesight can’t
acceptedAnswers: His eyesight can't be very good.
His eyesight can't be good.
His eyesight couldn't be very good.
His eyesight couldn't be good.

questions.prompt: He said he would ring, but he hasn’t. → He must
acceptedAnswers: He must have forgotten.
He must have forgotten to ring.
He must have forgotten about it.
He must have forgotten all about it.

questions.prompt: The last bus has already gone. → It must (+ comparative) than I thought.
acceptedAnswers: It must be later than I thought.

questions.prompt: I’m amazed that she married him so soon. → She can’t
questions.modelAnswer: She can’t have known him very long.
